title: Lee Bound Inference at a Zero Selection Gap with Pareto-Tailed Outcomes
banked_reason: Clean D0.5 math and decision PASS; normalized cold tier subfield with paper-score ceiling 7.0 below the 7.4 field floor; no bounded in-scope salvage.

The frontier requires known tail parameters, nonnegative outcomes, and a no-covariate randomized design, which limits its reach in applied Lee-bound settings.

The projection is mathematically defined, but no certified method for computing its extrema or worked application establishes its practical value; these limitations constrain the projected leading-journal score.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved the fractional Lee endpoint experiment, an honest finite-sample projection, and matched endpoint-pair and scalar excess-width rates across weak, detectable, and fixed selection gaps. The L-3 random-set wording was repaired without changing the projection or rates, and math and decision reviews passed with no findings; the normalized cold novelty grade nevertheless landed below the field floor. The F2 scaffold predates the source repair, so this bank preserves a sound discovery note rather than a completed Lean formalization; an independent tier adjudicator favored field and its dissent is recorded in the decision log.
tldr: Sharp endpoint inference at a sign-uncertain zero Lee selection gap has scale \(n^{-(\alpha-1)/(2\alpha)}\) for every finite-mean Pareto index \(\alpha>1\). An explicit Gaussian two-alternative lower envelope and the hybrid projection match at that weak-gap order. Over the known Pareto-envelope class, two-point witnesses also match both endpoint-pair diameter and whole-interval scalar excess width at rate \(\chi_\alpha(n)\) for fixed gaps and \(\chi_\alpha(n)+n^{-1/2}|\delta_n|^{-1/\alpha}\) around every detectable shrinking gap. At \(|\delta_n|=|c|n^{-\beta}\), the elbow is \(\beta=1-\alpha/2\) for \(1<\alpha<2\); every polynomially shrinking detectable gap is selection-dominated at and above two.
gap: The literature now establishes that sharp Lee bounds are irregular when selection effects can equal zero, but it does not quantify the endpoint experiment, minimax risk, or honest confidence-width cost generated by unbounded Pareto tails. Existing near-zero inference either uses bounded-outcome margin conditions, smooths to an outer target, or tests a different design-based null.
fill: Prove the exact local endpoint map and rate lower bounds on an explicit compatible causal submodel, then close the practical side with an honest Pareto-envelope projection whose random-count, measurability, and expected-diameter arguments are complete. The same procedure should link local, intermediate, and fixed-gap regimes without a sign pretest.
